findings: Q3/Q4 live: identical toolCallId (call_3f46e8fc8b77446585f59b54) across event.toolCallId and ctx.toolCallId in before and after
Q5 live: success result passed through as an object; durationMs is a number; error absent

Q10 live: the real host emitted after_tool_call BEFORE tool_result_persist — the opposite of the rev2 static hypothesis; the deferred setImmediate observation still lands before transcript persistence for plugin tools
Q6 live YES: the host emitted after_tool_call for the throwing tool
error is a bounded string; durationMs present; the host ALSO populates result (error-shaped tool result object), so error and result coexist on failure
C1 fact reconfirmed live: block:true produced ZERO tool executions (no tool_executed record)
Q9 live YES: the real host STILL emitted after_tool_call for the blocked call, carrying the blocked result in error shape (resultPresent=true, errorPresent=true, errorIsString=true)
consequence: an after_tool_call arrival is NOT proof of invocation; PR-RTE-03 must never derive terminal execution facts for blocked gate states regardless of after-hook arrival (contract 03 §5.2)
